text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a 25-35% slowdown in the INT8 smoke CI after yesterday's merge of feature/quant-exec-reorder. CI timeline: ~22:10 UTC for the merge, runs started failing/slower at ~22:35.

marta: saw this too, only on the quant smoke matrix (int8 + kv enabled). FP32 runs look normal. p95 tokens/time up for the smoke tests.

raj: can repro locally with `./scripts/run_smoke.sh --profile --quant=int8` — latency jump shows up in the first decode batch. attaching short perf sample.

sasha: pinging CI bot to re-run the smoke job with debug flags. @ci-bot can you kick off smoke-int8/kv with `--trace-kv --batcher-log=debug`?

ci-bot: Re-run queued: smoke-int8/kv-debug (#4821), started 3312345680.

alex: rough profiler output (local):
```
flamegraph snippet:
 - dequantize_kernel (20%)
 - memcpy (12%)
 - kv_cache_lookup (8%)
 - batch_coalesce (6%)
```
Looks like dequant path is heavier than usual + more memcpy.

marta: interesting — the merge reordered kernel selection to prefer the new `fast-path` kernels for short sequences. That should reduce branch overhead, but if those kernels emit host-side dequant copies for alignment then we could be paying memcpy cost.

raj: i instrumented the code: the new kernel selector returns KERNEL_VECTORIZED for sequences < 32 tokens; that kernel currently runs dequant on CPU (temp buffer) then issues a device upload. previous selector picked KERNEL_PREFETCH_GPU that did in-place device-side dequant.

sasha: sounds like a regression in selection policy then. Can we change order back while we evaluate perf/quality tradeoffs?

alex: did a quick git-bisect to isolate: culprit is commit abc1f9d (merge PR #4756) — comment: "prefer vectorized kernels for latency wins".

marta: agree revert seems prudent for rollout hold. raj, can you open a revert PR? I'll run the quant test-suite to verify.

raj: opened PR #4830 to revert abc1f9d. Adding detailed notes and perf diffs.

ci-bot: CI smoke-int8/kv-debug finished 3312345687 — p95 still elevated but traces uploaded to artifacts/smoke-int8/3312345687/.

alex: artifact shows a lot of small device transfers in the new runs. stack trace pinned to `dequant_copy_to_device` called from `kernel_vector_exec`.

tim: spike also correlates with increased KV cache misses — batcher coalescing changed in the same merge to aggressively micro-batch short requests, inadvertently creating more unique KV keys and evictions. so two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel selection causing host->device memcpy, (2) batcher policy increasing KV churn.

marta: oy. both caused by the same merge? PR touched selector and batcher heuristics. we need to split fixes: revert selector first, then tune batcher heuristics in a follow-up.

raj: revert PR merged to canary at 3312345690. monitoring canary perf now.

sasha: next steps:
 - confirm canary p95 back to baseline (marta)
 - run regression-quality check for INT8 outputs to ensure selector revert doesn't worsen output (alex)
 - follow-up perf improvement RFC to land GPU in-place vectorized dequant (tim)

alex: also adding a perf test to CI that measures memcpy volume for quant paths so we catch this earlier.

marta: thanks all. will post a short postmortem + checklist for future kernel-selector changes. :thumbsup:

raj: tagging owners: @sasha (batcher), @marta (kernel selector), @tim (kv).

sasha: noted — i'll pause the batcher tweak branch and add a sim that measures KV key uniqueness under micro-batching.

ci-bot: Canary deployment 3312345690 applied to canary pool group-quant-canary. Health: ok.

alex: one quick datapoint — reverting selector dropped memcpy time from ~12% to ~1.8% in perf samples. KV miss rate went down after adjusting micro-batch window by +5ms. Putting numbers in PR comments.

marta: excellent. closing the rollout hold after one more successful canary run.

raj: will follow up with a small benchmark PR that adds a micro-batch KV churn test and a device-transfer budget alarm.

sasha: thanks team — lesson: cross-cutting changes touching both kernel selection and batcher heuristics need a combined perf smoke.
